name: MO-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+19 partisan lean in a heavily Republican northwest Missouri seat
Polymarket prices the Republican at about 95%
Democrat Josh Smead has raised only ~$72k versus Stigall's ~$600k
Open seat removes incumbent risk but does not change the partisan fundamentals
model.rationale: The seat's R+19 lean, a 95% Republican market price, and a large fundraising gap leave no evidence pointing toward an upset, so the forecast stays near the fundamentals-based margin of roughly R+17.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Stigall underperforming the district's lean, or a surge of outside spending for Smead, would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Sam Graves (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Northwest Missouri's sixth district is one of the most Republican seats in the state, with a partisan lean of R+19. Sam Graves is retiring, so the seat is open, but the Republican nominee Chris Stigall enters as the heavy favorite. Polymarket prices the Republican at roughly 95%, and no expert raters list the race as competitive.

The money gap is stark: Stigall has raised about $600,000 while Democrat Josh Smead has raised under $75,000, with no outside support on the Democratic side. A Libertarian candidate is on the ballot but is not a factor. The forecast expects a Republican win by a wide, double-digit margin consistent with the district's fundamentals.
